claims.claim: The distal layer of ODF2 lies in close proximity to the core DAP protein CEP83 (~60 nm proximal to SCLT1).
claims.source: The proximal layer of ODF2 is at the lowest position among the sDAP proteins studied; while the distal layer of ODF2 lies in close proximity to the core DAP protein CEP83 (i.e. ~60 nm proximal to SCLT1 as we previously reported; Yang et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on imaging data and cites a previous study (Yang et al., 2018).

claims.claim: The distal layer CEP89 lies at the distal end of DAPs.

claims.claim: The proximal layer of CEP89 is proximal to CEP83 and lies in the sDAP region.

claims.evidence: The claim is based on imaging data shown in Figure 3d and e.

claims.claim: The dual localization of ODF2 and CEP89 suggests a potential structural relationship between sDAPs and DAPs.
claims.source: These observations suggest a potential structural relationship between sDAPs and DAPs.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the dual localization patterns observed in the imaging data.

claims.claim: In DAP or sDAP knockout cells, single-layered ODF2 was observed.
claims.source: Surprisingly, in DAP or sDAP knockout cells, single-layered ODF2 was observed (Figure 4b and e).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of knockout cells shown in Figure 4b and e.

claims.claim: The proximal layer of ODF2 was absent upon CEP128 depletion.
claims.source: In particular, the proximal layer of ODF2 was absent upon CEP128 depletion, where SCLT1 was used as a reference of the longitudinal position.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP128 knockout cells shown in Figure 4b.

claims.claim: In wild-type cells, ODF2-C distribution is wider than ODF2-N distribution in the radial direction.
claims.source: dSTORM imaging of ODF2-C revealed that in wild-type cells, ODF2-C distribution is wider than ODF2-N distribution in the radial direction (Figure 4b, c and d).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging comparing two different ODF2 antibodies shown in Figure 4b, c and d.

claims.claim: The distal edge of ODF2-C is closer to SCLT1 than that of ODF2-N, reaching further toward the centriole distal end.
claims.source: In addition, the distal edge of ODF2-C is closer to SCLT1 than that of ODF2-N, reaching further toward the centriole distal end.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging comparing two different ODF2 antibodies shown in Figure 4b, c and d.

claims.claim: When CEP128 is depleted, distributions of both ODF2-N and ODF2-C become thinner.
claims.source: Interestingly, when CEP128 is depleted, distributions of both ODF2-N and ODF2-C become thinner.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP128 knockout cells shown in Figure 4c and d.

claims.claim: The gap between ODF2-N/C and SCLT1 of CEP128–/– cells is larger than that of the wild-type cells.
claims.source: The gap between ODF2-N/C and SCLT1 of CEP128–/– cells is larger than that of the wild-type cells, illustrating both narrowing and shifting of ODF2 occupancy upon sDAP CEP128 depletion.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP128 knockout cells shown in Figure 4c and d.

claims.claim: CEP128, as the binding partner of ODF2, regulates the organization of ODF2.
claims.source: These observations imply that CEP128, as the binding partner of ODF2 (Kashihara et al., 2019), regulates the organization of ODF2.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from imaging data and cites a previous study (Kashihara et al., 2019).

claims.claim: In CEP83-depleted centrioles, one layer of ODF2 was absent.
claims.source: Similarly, in CEP83-depleted centrioles, one layer of ODF2 was absent (Figure 4e).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP83 knockout cells shown in Figure 4e.

claims.claim: ODF2 is associated with both DAPs and sDAPs as a downstream protein of CEP83 and CEP128, respectively.
claims.source: This observation implies that ODF2 is associated with both DAPs and sDAPs as a downstream protein of CEP83 and CEP128, respectively.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the knockout experiments showing loss of ODF2 layers upon depletion of CEP83 or CEP128.

claims.claim: The finding of one layer of ODF2 as a downstream protein of CEP128 explains previous genetic studies showing reduced ODF2 levels due to CEP128 depletion.

claims.evidence: The claim connects current findings with previous genetic studies (Mazo et al., 2016).

claims.claim: The proximal layer of CEP89 was absent when sDAP was depleted.
claims.source: Intriguingly, the proximal layer of CEP89 was absent when sDAP was depleted (Figure 4f and g).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP128 knockout cells shown in Figure 4f and g.

claims.claim: CEP89 signal was reduced when DAP was depleted as compared to that in the wild type cells.

claims.evidence: The claim is based on immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Similar to ODF2, CEP89 has dual roles associated with both DAPs and sDAPs.
claims.source: That is, similar to ODF2, CEP89 has dual roles associated with both DAPs and sDAPs.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the knockout experiments showing effects on CEP89 localization upon depletion of either DAPs or sDAPs.

claims.claim: In DAP-depleted CEP83–/–cells, ninein at the sDAPs covers a longitudinal region larger than that in wild-type cells.

claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of CEP83 knockout cells shown in Figure 4h and i.

claims.claim: The broadened longitudinal region of ninein spans from the sDAP region to the region originally occupied by DAPs.
claims.source: Using CP110 as a reference to indicate the distal boundary of the centriole, we find that the broadened longitudinal region of ninein spans from the sDAP region to the region originally occupied by DAPs.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging using CP110 as a reference marker shown in Figure 4h and i.

claims.claim: When CEP83 is stably expressed in CEP83–/– cells (CEP83–/– Rescue), the sDAP distribution of ninein is restored.
claims.source: In addition, when CEP83 is stably expressed in CEP83–/–cells (CEP83–/– Rescue), the sDAP distribution of ninein is restored (Figure 4h and i).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on dSTORM imaging of rescue cells shown in Figure 4h and i.

claims.claim: In wild-type cells, sDAPs mostly maintained their longitudinal position close to and proximal to the DAPs, but their shapes varied in different centrioles or even in the same centriole.

claims.claim: The sDAP structure is much less stable when DAPs are missing.

claims.claim: The absence of ninein reduced microtubule (MT) regrowth after nocodazole-induced MT depolymerization.

claims.claim: In widefield images, no observable difference is found in terms of centrioles serving as the center of MT networks between wild-type and CEP128–/– RPE-1 cells during the serum-starved G0 phase.

claims.claim: By overlaying multiple lateral super-resolved α-tubulin images of wild-type and CEP128–/–cells, a void region of MTs in the sDAP region of CEP128–/– cells was found.

claims.evidence: The claim is based on super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 5e, f and g.

claims.evidence: The claim is based on the super-resolution imaging data and cites a previous EM study (Mogensen et al., 2000).

claims.claim: The study illustrates a direct role for sDAP in MT anchoring.
claims.source: It illustrates a direct role for sDAP in MT anchoring.
claims.evidence: This is concluded from the super-resolution imaging showing loss of MTs at sDAPs upon CEP128 depletion.

claims.claim: Lateral-view images show another subset of MTs that terminate at the DAP region.

claims.evidence: The claim is based on super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 5e and f.

claims.claim: DAP-associated MTs do not seem to be affected by sDAP depletion.
claims.source: These DAP-associated MTs do not seem to be affected by sDAP depletion.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the imaging data comparing wild-type and CEP128 knockout cells.

claims.claim: γ-tubulins are highly enriched close to the centriole.

claims.evidence: The claim is based on super-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 6a.

claims.claim: The diameter of the γ-tubulin occupied region is about 400 nm, larger than the diameter of the centriole.
claims.source: The diameter of the γ-tubulin occupied region is about 400 nm, larger than the diameter of the centriole (Figure 6b).

results.result: The manuscript provides background on centrosome structure, DAPs, and sDAPs, citing established knowledge and prior studies. These claims establish the scientific context for the current work.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C29 are primarily citations to prior work and established knowledge about centrosome biology, DAP and sDAP structure, function, and protein composition. These background claims are well-supported by appropriate citations and represent accepted knowledge in the field.

results.result: The study systematically characterized sDAP molecular architecture using dSTORM super-resolution microscopy, mapped spatial organization of sDAP proteins, found structural coupling between DAPs and sDAPs, and observed the role of sDAPs in MT anchoring and γ-tubulin involvement in MT templating.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C34 describe the main objectives and findings of the study. These are supported by the extensive experimental data presented in the manuscript, including dSTORM imaging, knockout experiments, and quantitative analyses shown in multiple figures.

results.result: sDAP protein ring occupancy varies with cell cycle phase, with CEP170 showing wider radial distributions under serum-fed conditions and CEP128 showing incomplete ring occupancy that improves under serum starvation. sDAPs may not always possess nine-fold symmetry like DAPs.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C38 are supported by quantitative dSTORM imaging data shown in Figure 1, including statistical analyses comparing serum-fed and serum-starved conditions. The data demonstrate cell cycle-dependent variations in sDAP organization.

results.result: Different sDAP proteins occupy distinct radial positions, with ODF2 closest to the centriole wall (~200 nm diameter) and ninein/CEP170 at the periphery (~600 nm diameter). The size of protein distribution correlates with assembly hierarchy. TEM confirms nine-fold arrangement of sDAP stems, which are wider and more flexible than DAP stems.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C46 are supported by dSTORM diameter measurements (Figure 1g-h), correlation with assembly hierarchy data from prior studies, TEM imaging (Figure 1i), and 3D expansion microscopy (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). The measurements are quantitative and reproducible.

results.result: Lateral dSTORM imaging reveals the longitudinal organization of sDAP proteins: ODF2 forms two layers (~100 nm and ~200 nm proximal to SCLT1), CEP128 is sandwiched between them (~160 nm proximal), centriolin is above, and ninein/CEP170 localize radially outward. The composite structure is triangular and symmetric.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C57 are supported by dual-color lateral dSTORM imaging data shown in Figure 2a-d, with quantitative measurements of longitudinal and radial positions. The triangular structural model is derived from composite imaging data and is consistent with EM observations.

results.result: Both ODF2 and CEP89 exhibit dual-layer localization, with ODF2 layers at the proximal and distal ends of sDAP roots, and CEP89 layers at the distal DAP region and proximal sDAP region. This dual localization suggests structural relationships between DAPs and sDAPs.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C63 are supported by dSTORM imaging data shown in Figure 3d-e, with quantitative measurements of layer positions. The inference of structural relationships is reasonable based on the spatial overlap of these proteins between DAP and sDAP regions.

results.result: Knockout experiments reveal that ODF2 localization is differentially regulated by DAPs and sDAPs. CEP128 depletion removes the proximal ODF2 layer, while CEP83 depletion removes one layer. Different ODF2 antibodies show distinct localization patterns, and CEP128 regulates ODF2 organization.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C73 are supported by dSTORM imaging of CEP128 and CEP83 knockout cells (Figure 4a-e), immunoblotting confirmation of knockouts, and comparison of two different ODF2 antibodies. The data demonstrate differential regulation of ODF2 by DAP and sDAP proteins.

results.result: CEP89 has dual roles associated with both DAPs and sDAPs. The proximal layer of CEP89 is absent when sDAPs are depleted (CEP128 knockout), and CEP89 signal is reduced when DAPs are depleted (CEP83 knockout).
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C76 are supported by dSTORM imaging of CEP128 knockout cells (Figure 4f-g) and immunofluorescence imaging of CEP83 knockout cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). The data demonstrate that CEP89 localization depends on both DAP and sDAP integrity.

results.result: DAP depletion (CEP83 knockout) causes ninein to spread longitudinally from the sDAP region toward the centriole distal end, and this is rescued by CEP83 re-expression. TEM shows that sDAP structure becomes highly variable and unstable when DAPs are missing, demonstrating structural coupling between DAPs and sDAPs.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C83 are supported by dSTORM imaging of CEP83 knockout and rescue cells (Figure 4h-i), TEM of wild-type and CEP83 knockout cells (Figure 4j), and quantitative analysis. The rescue experiment provides strong evidence for specificity. The TEM data directly demonstrate structural instability of sDAPs upon DAP loss.

results.result: Super-resolution imaging reveals that CEP128 knockout (sDAP depletion) creates a void region of microtubules specifically in the sDAP region, providing direct evidence that sDAPs anchor a subset of MTs. DAP-associated MTs are not affected by sDAP depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C90 are supported by widefield imaging (Figure 5a-b), axial dSTORM imaging (Figure 5c-d), and lateral composite dSTORM imaging of α-tubulin (Figure 5e-g). The overlay of multiple images clearly shows MT loss at the sDAP region in CEP128 knockout cells. This is the first high-resolution imaging evidence for sDAP-mediated MT anchoring.

results.result: γ-tubulins are enriched around the mother centriole in a well-defined cylindrical distribution (~400 nm diameter) from the proximal end to the sDAP level, leaving the DAP-sDAP region less populated. This distribution differs from α-tubulin enrichment at sDAPs, suggesting at least two populations of γ-tubulins: one for MT anchoring at sDAPs and another along the centriole not associated with α-tubulin.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C97 are supported by lateral and axial dSTORM imaging of γ-tubulin (Figure 6a-b), diameter measurements, and comparison with α-tubulin distribution. The inference of two γ-tubulin populations is reasonable based on the spatial mismatch between γ-tubulin and α-tubulin distributions.

results.result: CEP128 knockout causes statistically significant reduction of γ-tubulin at sDAP tips and allows γ-tubulin to spread distally toward the DAP region. This distal γ-tubulin population may not anchor MTs, as decreased α-tubulin is observed at the distal end. sDAPs spatially regulate the distal boundary of γ-tubulins along the centriole.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C101 are supported by statistical analysis of γ-tubulin intensity in wild-type and CEP128 knockout cells (Figure 6c-f). The inference that distal γ-tubulins don't anchor MTs is reasonable given the decreased α-tubulin at that location, though this involves some speculation.

results.result: The study demonstrates that DAPs and sDAPs are structurally coupled despite their distinct functions. sDAP proteins are less organized than DAP proteins. ODF2 and CEP128 form a protein complex. DAPs serve as a distal border for sDAPs, and sDAP structural arrangement depends on DAP structure. The study provides direct evidence for sDAP-mediated MT anchoring and clarifies ninein's role.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C115 are summary statements of the study's main findings, supported by the comprehensive experimental data including dSTORM imaging, knockout experiments, TEM, and quantitative analyses presented throughout the manuscript. The conclusions are well-supported by converging lines of evidence.

results.result: The manuscript speculates about potential functions of sDAP-anchored MTs (mechanosensation, Golgi bridging) and the major γ-tubulin population (MT nucleation reservoir). These are presented as hypotheses for future investigation.
results.evaluation: Claims C102, C116-C125 are explicitly speculative, involving hypotheses about functional roles that are not directly tested in the current study. While these speculations are reasonable based on the data and prior knowledge, they require additional experiments for validation. The authors appropriately present these as possibilities rather than conclusions.

results.result: Prior studies showed that ninein absence reduces MT regrowth, that sDAP removal doesn't affect ciliogenesis, and that sDAP proteins localize even when DAPs are depleted.
results.evaluation: Claims C84, C111-C112 cite prior published work to provide context for the current findings. These are appropriately referenced and represent established knowledge from previous studies.
